Claude is my home base. It runs most of my work.

For these 15 jobs though, I reach elsewhere:

Making images → ChatGPT and Nano Banana
Real photos and artwork from a prompt.

Making videos → Higgsfield
Turns your text into video clips.

Avatar videos → HeyGen
A presenter reads your script.

Recording video → Tella
Records your screen and camera at once.

Voiceovers → ElevenLabs
Natural-sounding AI narration.

Voice dictation → Wispr Flow
You talk, it types for you.

Video analysis → Gemini
Reads and sums up any video.

Meeting notes → Granola
Writes up your meetings for you.

Live answers → Perplexity
Up-to-the-minute web results.

Research your sources → NotebookLM
Answers built from your own documents.

Docs and knowledge base → Notion
Where all your work lives.

Open source → Ollama and GLM
Capable models you can run for cheap.

Coding → Codex
OpenAI's answer to Claude Code.

Operations → Hermes
My WhatsApp agent that keeps the pipeline moving.

Automation → Zapier
Automates the work between all my apps.

I do not open all 15 every week.

But knowing which tool wins which job is the game.

Claude for most of it. These for the rest.

Which one would you add?

Every tool linked in the first comment 👇

content:
UPDATE: Fatima Khan is back 🔥

Thank you everyone for your support!!

— 

I need your help!

A dear friend and business partner of mine has been logged out of her LinkedIn account.

Fatima Khan co-founded the AI Creators Club with me.
We taught 100+ people together through our bootcamp.

She's been locked out since Friday.

There was no ban, strike or rule broken.

LinkedIn's identity check just won't accept her photos.
Same error every time: "Can't verify photos."

I've lost an account three times this year.
Instagram twice. LinkedIn once.

Every time it's the same:

- You find out by trying to log in
- There's no human to appeal to
- The form tells you nothing

Both times it was an algorithm deciding.

This is a problem. Since Meta's layoffs, hundreds of thousands of accounts have lost access despite being legitimate creators helping people. 

What got me back wasn't the appeal.
It was other people filing support tickets.

Before you scroll, this takes two minutes:

1. Go to https://lnkd.in/ebgM7sgt
2. Select "Other"
3. Type anything in the search box and hit enter
4. Scroll to the bottom and click "Create a support ticket"
5. Paste this into the form:

"Hi LinkedIn Support, I am writing to vouch for Fatima Khan (fatima-rasheed-khan), case number 260723-029352.

Fatima is a legitimate creator with over 100,000 followers and her account is central to her business. She cannot regain access because the Persona identity verification repeatedly fails with a 'Can't verify photos' error.

She has tried multiple devices, browsers, lighting conditions and government-issued IDs, so this is a technical fault rather than a question of her identity. Please prioritise her case and escalate it to the Account Recovery team for a manual review."

One ticket does nothing. Two hundred moves a queue.

Repost ♻️ so someone at LinkedIn sees this.

P.S. Has your account ever been suspended?

#BringBackFatima

Claude Code (actually) runs all 4 of my channels.

The exact system behind 350k+ across socials:

Check this out before you build your own:

Watch here → https://lnkd.in/eXTx_FbB
Read here → https://lnkd.in/ezgyjNPN

Step 1: Every idea gets pre-validated

Ideas come from 3 places:
- X shows what is trending now.
- Reddit shows what people care about.
- Instagram shows what my audience saves.

Hermes then scores and ranks each one.
Only pre-validated ideas get made.

Step 2: One brief, one operator

The winning idea becomes a tight brief.
One idea, one angle, one outcome.

Claude Code runs every channel from there.
One operator, one standard, every channel.

Step 3: LinkedIn (infographics)

- A strategist agent finds the angle.
- Claude Code builds the graphic in HTML.
- A cold QA agent scores it to 95.
- Notion stores and logs the asset.

Step 4: Instagram (reels)

- Claude drafts the hooks, I pick one.
- I record it on camera.
- Higgsfield adds the B-roll.
- ManyChat auto-DMs the free guide.

Step 5: YouTube (long-form)

- I record screen and camera in Tella.
- HyperFrames handles the full edit.
- GPT Image 2 builds the thumbnail.
- YouTube publishes the video.

Step 6: Newsletter (Substack)

- Agent Browser researches and drafts.
- Voice skills keep it sounding like me.
- Claude writes the subject line.
- Substack ships it to subscribers.

Step 7: Notion holds everything

Every asset, queue and metric lives here.
One source of truth for me and the team.

Step 8: The data picks what is next

Apify pulls reach, saves and comments.
The numbers choose the next idea, not my gut.

Here is what the system really does:

Each tool owns one job, and only one:
- Hermes scores and ranks the ideas.
- Claude Code builds every graphic.
- Higgsfield fills the B-roll I never shot.
- HyperFrames edits the whole video.
- GPT Image 2 makes every thumbnail.
- Apify tells me what actually landed.
- Notion holds every asset and metric.

30+ posts a week, across 4 channels.
Claude runs the process, I make the calls.

The tools do not create the content.
They let me ship what I never could alone.

content:
85% of leaders regretted a major decision last year.

I've coached 650+ CEOs.
Every one of them has been there.
And I have too, of course.

The decision that keeps you up at 2am.
The one you overthought until the window closed.
The one you rushed when you should have slowed down.

The gap between a good call and a costly one is preparation.

The best CEOs pick their decision tool before the pressure hits.

7 decision frameworks worth keeping close:

1/ The Eisenhower Matrix
→ Sort by urgency and importance
→ Do it, schedule it, delegate it, or delete it

2/ The OODA Loop
→ Observe, Orient, Decide, Act
→ Built for fighter pilots. Works for fast markets.

3/ One-Way vs. Two-Way Doors
→ Reversible? Move fast.
→ Irreversible? Slow down.

4/ The ICE Method
→ Score options by Impact, Confidence, and Ease
→ Pick the highest score. Stop debating.

5/ The SPADE Framework
→ One person decides. Everyone else is heard.
→ Kills the "who's actually in charge" problem.

6/ The Premortem
→ Assume the decision already failed
→ Work backward. Fix it before you commit.

7/ The 10/10/10 Rule
→ How will you feel in 10 minutes, 10 months, 10 years?
→ Strips the emotion out of the decision.

That last one is the one I lean on most.

10 minutes in, you're scared.
10 months later, you're glad you did it.
10 years later, you've made that call 20 times.

You're bulletproof.
